study_identification_part.si4_title: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with FirstEpisode Psychosis Using Normative Models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To characterize the temporal evolution of cortical correlates of psychosis and their associations with symptoms over a 10-year period using normative models, and to demonstrate the utility of transfer learning for longitudinal MRI feature comparison across different scanners in schizophrenia patients.

nm1_model_origin.detail: Pre-trained on pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets (77 sites, 40435 participants) using HBR with age, sex, and scanner ID as predictors. Adapted to 3 unseen Oslo scanners by transferring hyperparameters as informed priors, using held-out cross-sectional data from controls for adaptation.
nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: Using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites, and 40 435 participants, the reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set of 2548 CTRL and patients (5%, stratified by sites). We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners, by transferring the (hyper) parameters as informed priors for these new sites. For this adaptation step, we used held-out cross-sectional data from CTRL from these 3 scanners, following methods described previously 55 (supplementary table 1).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear Mixed Effects models (LME) were used to investigate the impact of diagnosis, time, age, and sex on deviation scores, and associations between deviation scores and PANSS scores. Non-parametric Wilcoxon tests were used for group differences in extreme deviations. Benjamini-Hochberg procedure (FDR corrected, α = 0.05) was applied for multiple comparison correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study found a diffuse pattern of cortical thickness atypicalities in schizophrenia early in the illness course that attenuated over time, with associations between these deviations and clinical symptoms, suggesting normative models can track clinical trajectories.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study identified a diffuse pattern of cortical thickness (CT) atypicalities in schizophrenia spectrum disorders that attenuated over a 10-year period. Specifically, LMEs showed significant diagnosis and time × diagnosis interaction effects in cortical deviations, with baseline Cohen's d for median CT deviation at -0.46, reducing to -0.27 at 10-year follow-up. Significant group differences in extreme negative deviations were found at baseline (P = 2.56 × 10^-5, CL effect size = 66%) and at 12 months (P = .0006, CL effect size = 63%), but not at the third time point. PANSS scores significantly decreased over time (e.g., total PANSS: baseline-10-year Cohen's d = -0.87). Associations were found between CT deviations and PANSS scores, including anterior cingulate gyrus with PANSS total (coefficient = -4.0, P = .003) and general, and insular and orbitofrontal regions with PANSS negative scores.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Potential recruitment bias and attrition bias; inability to directly test the differential effects of first- and second-generation antipsychotics due to small sample of first-generation users; extreme deviations may reflect factors other than schizophrenia pathology (e.g., noise, medication, comorbidities); moderate sample size at the third follow-up could bias findings; potential influence of different scanners across study waves.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, even with access to the national registry data, ensuring representative recruitment in clinical and population-based cohorts is nontrivial...Second, whilst our findings are suggestive that second-generation antipsychotics may have different chronic effects on brain structure to first-generation antipsychotics, we were unable to test this directly...Third, extreme cortical deviations may not only relate to schizophrenia-related pathologies but could also be markers of other effects...Finally, we acknowledge that our sample size at the third follow-up session is moderate...Also, despite best efforts, the inclusion of different scanners across different waves of the study may have influenced our findings.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study demonstrated the utility of transfer learning from large-scale reference normative models for making meaningful comparisons of MRI features across different scanners in a longitudinal setting.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study utilized a 10-year longitudinal cohort from the TOP study. Registry data were used for healthcare information. Findings suggest that the observed attenuation of cortical differences over time is not consistent with a simple neurodegenerative model of schizophrenia.
